comparator.name: Computer Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted regulations define an English full-time general degree with no formal specialization. Year one has 60 EC required. Year two combines 45 EC required with separate 3, 6 and 6 EC constrained choices in periods 3, 5 and 6. This example uses Academic Writing, Introduction to Computer Security and Human-Computer Interaction respectively. Algorithms II, not the repeated Algorithms I wording on the programme overview, is required. Year three has 30 EC of open study and 30 EC required, including the 15 EC Bachelor Project. The English test and any required refresher carry no extra credits. Article 9.1 requires prior Computer Programming or Systems Programming Project for Object-Oriented and Functional Programming and Operating Systems. A specified earlier two-course programming sequence also qualifies for the former. Project admission requires 120 EC from the Computer Science bachelor. Project work may be individual or in a group. Two examiners assess technical work, thesis and presentation individually, weighted 50%, 40% and 10%, with at least 5.5 in each.

alternatives.concept: Builds software and investigates how it runs. Python, C++ and Haskell support programming projects, while algorithms, networks, operating systems and databases develop ways to analyze and implement computing systems. Mathematics and machine learning extend that foundation. Consumer product design adds practice in investigating user needs and developing prototypes.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses (30 EC) differ in each direction. Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Robotics deepen mathematical modeling and autonomous motion, and Introduction to Brain & Behavior adds a human-context foundation. The first option uses those places for software development, advanced algorithms, consumer product design and ethics.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Both options offer substantial programming, algorithms, systems and mathematics. The second option uses advanced mathematics and robotics to give intelligent systems a different focus. The available courses do not support a third specialist sequence in security or bioinformatics, or subject didactics and classroom practice in computing. The software option already addresses advanced programming.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop computational problem-solving, programming, testing and debugging. UCR teaches these through Python.
Both teach formal logic, sets and proof. UCR also applies these ideas to recursive structures and games.
Both study matrices, linear transformations and related mathematical methods. UCR applies them to signals and data.
Both develop probability and statistical inference for computational work. UCR uses simulations and sampling projects.
Both develop algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis. UCR includes programming investigations.
Both use greedy methods, dynamic programming and network flows. UCR also emphasizes algebraic algorithms and implementation experiments.
Both develop calculus methods for computing. UCR teaches discrete logic and proof separately.
UCR studies historical philosophical arguments. VU teaches the history of science in a dedicated computer science course.
UCR covers computability and complexity within Algorithms & Data Structures. VU requires a separate course on automata and complexity.
Both study network layers, protocols and internet communication. UCR shares the course with operating-system topics.
Both study relational data, SQL and query processing. UCR also covers normalization and authorization.
Both study object-oriented and functional programming. UCR builds projects in C++ and Haskell.
Both ask ethical questions about computing. UCR focuses on AI, including fairness, privacy and responsibility.
UCR covers operating systems and network infrastructure. VU separately studies computer architecture and organization.
UCR’s product design course investigates user needs for physical products. VU teaches formal software requirements engineering.
UCR robotics studies motion and manipulation. VU teaches embedded systems through an integrated hardware and software project.
UCR develops programming through several course projects. VU requires a separate systems programming project.
UCR studies networks, databases and programming. VU gives web application technologies dedicated attention.
UCR applies design patterns and testing in Software Development. VU has a separate Software Design course.
UCR covers scheduling, concurrency and memory in Networks & Operating Systems. VU teaches these in a dedicated operating systems course.
UCR develops academic writing in Personal & Professional Development and Rhetorical Communication. VU offers a dedicated computer science writing choice.
UCR studies product design or human cognition, depending on the option. VU’s selected course focuses on designing and evaluating interactions with computer systems.
UCR touches on database authorization and AI privacy. VU’s selected course studies computer security directly.
Both teach statistical learning and prediction. UCR uses regression, classification and model validation in practical data projects.
The 30 EC are open for a minor or an approved elective package.
VU requires a supervised scientific computing project. UCR’s optional independent research is additional to its scheduled coursework.

notes.text: VU gives dedicated attention to computer hardware, web technology, embedded systems, systems programming and automata. This VU example also includes security and interaction design. UCR covers related concepts across several courses and offers less specialist depth in those areas.
VU requires a 15 EC supervised scientific project with a thesis and presentation. UCR includes projects within courses. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Computer Science combines programming and software engineering with algorithms, formal reasoning, mathematics, computer systems, networks, data and AI. Its general bachelor includes constrained second-year options, an open academic semester and a supervised scientific CS project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options teach programming, algorithms, computer systems, mathematics and machine learning. The first adds more software development and advanced algorithms. The second adds linear systems, advanced calculus and robotic motion planning.

curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC example includes three restricted second-year choices and 30 EC of open study in year three. Students need 120 EC from the Computer Science bachelor before starting the 15 EC project. They can work individually or in a group. Two examiners assess each student’s technical contribution, thesis and presentation.

componentNotes.y2-09: Selected writing option, 3 EC in period 3.
componentNotes.y2-10: Selected interaction design option, 6 EC in period 6.
componentNotes.y2-11: Selected security option, 6 EC in period 5.
componentNotes.y3-01: Open study can include a minor, an approved elective package or study abroad.
componentNotes.y3-03: A supervised scientific computing project assessed individually.
